headline_stat.name: unit 471 circular-linear phase-position correlation (rho, permutation p)
headline_stat.value: rho=0.53, p=0.008 (README says 0.010), slope=-221 deg/rad, n=32

stated_limitation: Three additional candidate place cells show negative precession slopes in the same direction but do not reach significance individually (p = 0.25-0.39), consistent with the limited sampling of a single session (18 laps).

justification.dataset: DANDI:000059 is a canonical Buzsáki-lab dorsal-CA1 maze recording on the known-good list for theta precession, exactly the standard choice.
justification.handling: Real data streamed from S3, LFP decimated correctly from a dedicated theta-reference channel, position linearized per lap, and unit/place-cell inclusion criteria are explicit and defensible.
justification.analysis: Kempter circular-linear regression with a position-shuffle permutation null is the correct method with the required control and proper circular statistics.
justification.correctness: The exemplar numbers reproduce and are internally consistent with the figure, with a minor README-vs-figure p discrepancy (0.010 vs 0.008) and no other traceability problem.
justification.figures: Figures show the effect clearly for unit 471 with labeled units and sample sizes, and the exemplar is chosen by correlation strength (the effect itself), not by fitted slope.
justification.honesty: The headline (unit 471) is genuine and honestly caveated, but the population sentence overstates consistency by calling three cells 'negative in the same direction' when unit 517 is positive (+42 deg/rad, p=0.583) and quoting a p-range that excludes it, a claim contradicted by its own figure.
justification.verdict: The core precession result is sound and well-executed, but the mischaracterized population trend and the p discrepancy need correction before the write-up can be believed as stated.
